title: Inferno MELEE ONLY (No bloodfury)
summary: A full melee-only Inferno completion, recorded at about two hours long with chapters for the waves, a single Jad, triple Jads and Zuk. The transcript is almost empty, so this note is based on the description and chapters: Gnomonkey found it much easier than expected, forgot Amulet of blood fury existed and did not go for speed.

claims.text: Gnomonkey completed the Inferno using melee only in a roughly two-hour video (July 2021), with chapters for boring waves, harder waves, a single Jad, triple Jads and Zuk.
Gnomonkey says the melee-only Inferno was a lot easier than he expected it to be.
Gnomonkey says he genuinely forgot Amulet of blood fury exists in the melee-only Inferno run, and that he probably would have saved money on blood runes if he had used it.
Gnomonkey did not go for speed records in the melee-only Inferno; he says he had a nice chill time.
Gnomonkey says in hindsight he should have brought another stamina potion and cheesed with the Saradomin godsword a bit less in the melee-only Inferno.
The melee-only video splits the Inferno into boring waves (0:00 to 51:16), harder waves (51:17 to 1:45:29), a single Jad (1:45:30), triple Jads (1:48:41) and Zuk (1:56:39).
Gnomonkey's melee-only Inferno run lasted about 2 hours 3 minutes, with the Zuk fight starting at 1:56:39.
